learning: If line loss stays at zero and max_error falls below about 0.058 m, the entry transient was tied to look-ahead. If max_error stays at 0.061 m, the excursion is a fixed or start-up effect that neither look-ahead nor gain can remove. If line loss returns, a shorter look-ahead is not usable at this span.
notes: Iteration 2 controller on the Builder's y = 0.02 row, with no other changes. It isolates the look-ahead change, since kp, ki, kd and line recovery all match the best-scoring design. Report line_loss_events and max_error per track, and whether the excursion occurs at the start of the run or at a specific bend.
rationale: The Builder's y = 0.02 proposal keeps the best-scoring pairing from iteration 2 (16 mm sensors at x = ±0.05 m, kp 3.5, ki 0, kd 0.05, base_speed 1.6, last_direction recovery, weights [-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1]). The only geometry change is sensor y, moving from 0.04 m to 0.02 m. Evidence: iteration 2 (y 0.04) gave zero line loss on oval and slalom and max_error of about 0.061 m. Iteration 3 (y 0.06 with ki 0.3) brought line loss back on the s-bend and slalom and left max_error unchanged. Iteration 4 (wheel_track 0.15, kp 4.4) and iteration 5 (mass 0.6) left max_error at about 0.061 m. Across all controller and geometry changes, max_error has stayed at about 0.061 m, so the excursion does not look like a gain, footprint, span or mass limit. A start-up or entry transient is the most likely cause. The controller therefore stays at the iteration 2 values, so the race isolates the look-ahead change. I do not add ki, because iteration 3 confounded it with y. I do not change kp, because kp 3.0, 3.5 and 4.4 all gave the same max_error. Mass stays at 0.8 kg, as the Builder specified. I expect line_loss_events to stay at zero and max_error to move only if the shorter look-ahead changes the entry transient. This is a prediction, not a measurement.
